jobs.description: Adjunct Faculty, Public Health Essential Job Functions Life University seeks applicants for an Adjunct Faculty to serve in our new Bachelor of Science degree program in Public Health. Our public health program emphasizes wellness, prevention, service, and community engagement within a population health framework. Supporting the University’s mission and vision, the program will approach public health as the study and promotion of conditions that support human potential and reduce barriers to optimal health and well-being. We are seeking dynamic instructors who will bring a creative and student-centered approach to the classroom and online instruction. Once hired, Adjunct Faculty in public health will be invited to teach and develop courses as needed. Primarily responsible for the instruction, supervision, and evaluation of students in the classroom as well as course assessments for the department. Prepare a syllabus for each course taught using the college template. Teach class in a professional manner, teaching the material that is present in the syllabus and course outline. Start and end each class on time. Communicate your teaching and student office hours schedule for each quarter and be present virtually during student office hours. Appropriately maintain all necessary records for each course taught. Attend scheduled meetings and events as appropriate and as requested by Assistant Dean of Social Sciences. Cultivate in oneself and others a commitment to helpfulness, building relationships, collaborating to find the best solution, and serving students with care and integrity.

Fort Valley State University, the only 1890 land-grant university in Georgia, is a comprehensive institution that provides an education to over 2,800 students including graduate students. The university is located in the town of Fort Valley in Peach County, the original site of the state's peach industry. Its 1,365-acre (5.52 km2) campus is Georgia's second-largest public university in area. Fort Valley State University is an affirmative action, equal opportunity institution and does not discriminate against applicants, students, or employees on the basis of race, gender, ethnicity, national origin, sexual orientation, religion, age, disability, or marital or veteran status. JOB SUMMARY: This announcement is to assist in the building a pool of candidates for upcoming adjunct (part-time) opportunities within the Mathematics Program in the Department of Natural and Computational Sciences. Currently, we are recruiting for adjunct faculty to teach courses in College Algebra, Trigonometry, Precalculus, Calculus I, Elementary Statistics, Physics I, Physics II, Introduction to Linear Algebra, and any additional courses as needed by the Program. Courses will be offered in in-person, hybrid, and/or online modalities. DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: Teach undergraduate level Mathematics and related courses in a face-to-face, online, or hybrid format. Teach courses as assigned by the Department Chair and maintain University policies. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Master's Degree in Mathematics or related discipline. Ability to successfully pass a background check. Excellent analytical, oral, and written communication skills and teamwork. 2-3 years of experience at the university level. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Prior experience in teaching in College Algebra, Trigonometry, Precalculus, Calculus I, Elementary Statistics, Physics I, Physics II, and/or Introduction to Linear Algebra. Application Process: This position is open until filled. The finalists will be required to submit to a background investigation consistent with the policy of the University System of Georgia. Additional information about FVSU is available at http://www.fvsu.edu/. The application packet must include the following: A letter of interest that addresses the responsibilities and qualifications of the position. Current curriculum vitae. Undergraduate and graduate transcripts. At least three references with full contact information including emails. (References will not be contacted without consent from applicants) Additional information will be requested upon receipt of the application. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence, Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these standards. jobs.description: Young Harris College invites applications for an adjunct professor of Computer Science position beginning August 1, 2026. The successful candidate will have earned at least a Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology(IT), Information Systems(IS), or a related degree. Strong commitment to teaching in a liberal arts undergraduate curriculum is required. Candidate must be comfortable with technology and experience with Moodle is a plus. Duties will primarily include teaching CSCI 1100: Introduction to Personal Computing. This is an introductory course that describes how computers are applied to solving problems in our information-oriented society. Included is a study of fundamental hardware, operating systems, networking, computer privacy and security, and the social, economic, and legal impact of information systems. Standard business-based software packages (MS Office) are used by students to solve a variety of problems. This course is required for many of our science majors who use Excel in their coursework and is also an elective for a diverse set of students across campus. Applications should include a two-page cover letter that includes teaching experience and philosophy, a CV, transcripts and contact information for three references. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. Selected candidates must successfully pass a background check. Young Harris College is a private baccalaureate and master’s degree-granting institution located in the beautiful mountains of North Georgia. Founded in 1886 and historically affiliated with The United Methodist Church, Young Harris College educates, inspires, and empowers students through an education that purposefully integrates the liberal arts and professional studies. 1,400 students are enrolled in its residential and Early College programs. The College is an active member of the NCAA Division II and remains a fierce competitor in the prestigious Conference Carolinas. For more information, visit yhc.edu. Apply Now About Young Harris College Young Harris College is proud of its Wesleyan heritage and commitment. The College was founded by a Methodist circuit-rider, and its namesake and sustainer during the institution’s formative years was one of the state’s outstanding Methodist laypeople. For several years, all Presidents of the College were ordained Methodist ministers, with Young Harris later appointing professional educators who were active lay leaders in the Methodist Church to the presidency. Today, Young Harris is a member of the North American Association of Methodist Schools, Colleges, and Universities (NAAMSCU), a voluntary association of over 100 private schools, colleges, universities, and seminaries in the United States that cooperate to advance the common good of member institutions and to address issues of mutual concern to the church and the academy. Collaborate with faculty to collect, disaggregate, and analyze student performance and program data to support continuous improvement and accreditation requirements. Complete other duties as assigned. jobs.description: The Introduction to Construction is responsible for delivering classroom instruction and hands-on training for students enrolled in the Home Builders Institute (HBI) Pre-Apprenticeship Certificate Training (PACT) Core program. PACT Core is an industry-recognized introductory construction training program designed to prepare individuals for entry-level employment and apprenticeship opportunities in the residential construction and skilled trades industries. The instructor will teach foundational construction skills using the HBI PACT Core curriculum, which includes construction safety, OSHA awareness, tool identification and usage, construction math, blueprint reading, employability skills, communication, and an introduction to multiple construction trades. The program is designed to help students develop the technical knowledge, workplace readiness, and professional behaviors necessary for success in the construction industry. The ideal candidate will combine real-world construction experience with a passion for workforce development, student engagement, and career preparation. Key Responsibilities: Deliver HBI PACT Core curriculum in classroom and lab settings Teach foundational construction skills, safety procedures, and proper tool usage Provide hands-on training and supervise student skill development Monitor student attendance, performance, and progress Maintain a safe and organized learning environment Prepare students for industry-recognized credentials and employment opportunities

jobs.title: Adjunct Professor of Computer Science
jobs.description: Young Harris College invites applications for an adjunct professor of Computer Science position beginning August 1, 2026. The successful candidate will have earned at least a Master’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology(IT), Information Systems(IS), or a related degree. Strong commitment to teaching in a liberal arts undergraduate curriculum is required. Candidate must be comfortable with technology and experience with Moodle is a plus. Duties will primarily include teaching CSCI 1100: Introduction to Personal Computing. This is an introductory course that describes how computers are applied to solving problems in our information-oriented society. Included is a study of fundamental hardware, operating systems, networking, computer privacy and security, and the social, economic, and legal impact of information systems. Standard business-based software packages (MS Office) are used by students to solve a variety of problems. This course is required for many of our science majors who use Excel in their coursework and is also an elective for a diverse set of students across campus. Applications should include a two-page cover letter that includes teaching experience and philosophy, a CV, transcripts and contact information for three references. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until the position is filled. Selected candidates must successfully pass a background check. Young Harris College is a private baccalaureate and master’s degree-granting institution located in the beautiful mountains of North Georgia. Founded in 1886 and historically affiliated with The United Methodist Church, Young Harris College educates, inspires, and empowers students through an education that purposefully integrates the liberal arts and professional studies. 1,400 students are enrolled in its residential and Early College programs. The College is an active member of the NCAA Division II and remains a fierce competitor in the prestigious Conference Carolinas. For more information, visit yhc.edu. Apply Now About Young Harris College Young Harris College is proud of its Wesleyan heritage and commitment. The College was founded by a Methodist circuit-rider, and its namesake and sustainer during the institution’s formative years was one of the state’s outstanding Methodist laypeople. For several years, all Presidents of the College were ordained Methodist ministers, with Young Harris later appointing professional educators who were active lay leaders in the Methodist Church to the presidency. Today, Young Harris is a member of the North American Association of Methodist Schools, Colleges, and Universities (NAAMSCU), a voluntary association of over 100 private schools, colleges, universities, and seminaries in the United States that cooperate to advance the common good of member institutions and to address issues of mutual concern to the church and the academy. Young Harris is also a member of the University Senate of the UMC’s General Board of Higher Education and Ministry (GBHEM), making the institution eligible for funding from UMC agencies. Young Harris supports the UMC’s commitment to “open hearts, open minds, and open doors.” For more information about the College’s affiliation with GBEHM, follow this link: GBHEM. Young Harris College does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, national origin, sex , age, disability, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law. The university is located in the town of Fort Valley in Peach County, the original site of the state's peach industry. Its 1,365-acre (5.52 km2) campus is Georgia's second-largest public university in area. Fort Valley State University is an equal opportunity employer. The University does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or University System of Georgia policy. JOB SUMMARY: The College of Agriculture, Family Sciences and Technology (CAFST) seeks an energetic and student-focused faculty member with expertise in Plant Pathology for a 12-month research appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor. This is a hybrid position with appointment in Departments of Agricultural Research (75%) and Agricultural Sciences (25% instruction). The incumbent will be responsible for teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in Plant Science and Plant Pathology as determined by departmental needs. The faculty members will also play a key role in collaboratively reimagining existing plant science courses with faculty in both content and scope to ensure alignment with external stakeholders. Specific teaching assignments will be assigned by the Department Chair. The selected candidate will advise and mentor undergraduate and graduate students, support relevant student organizations and assist with the recruitment of students interested in plant sciences/plant pathology and related fields The successful candidate will be expected to develop a robust field-based research program which addresses diseases in economically important row crops, peaches, and pecans in Georgia. The faculty member is expected to establish relationships with stakeholders in Middle Georgia and develop an extramurally funded research program to address their needs, with a focus on developing strategies for reducing crop losses to disease. The research program must have a primary emphasis on agronomic field research evaluating management strategies that can readily implemented by producers, with a focus on major crops grown in Middle Georgia including cotton, peanut, blueberries, pecans and others. Responsibilities will include securing extramural funding to conduct field research that addresses economically important disease problems in the region; hiring and supervision of staff to initiate and complete studies; leading field research and associated data collection and analysis; disseminating results to farmers, crop advisors, agronomists and other stakeholders in the FVSU Cooperative Extension Service. collaborate with colleagues and agents in the Cooperative Extension at FVSU. Exposure to pesticides and chemicals is possible with this position. Candidates must obtain pesticide certification and wear prescribed PPE. As part of CAFST's commitment to developing and strengthening the plant science programs, the successful candidate will have access to start-up funds contingent upon submission of a competitive research plan. Position Details Position Information Job Type Faculty Position Title Assistant Professor of Visual Arts Position Number FV0006 Department Visual Art Location Morehouse College - Atlanta GA Position Summary The Division of Humanities, Social Science, Media and Arts (HSSMA) at Morehouse College invites applications for full-time Assistant Professor in Visual Arts (non-tenure-track) to start August 2027. Morehouse College is seeking innovators that lead students to creative outlets for further exposition of the Visual Arts through studio and lecture courses surrounding contemporary issues in the field that are accessible to broad audiences of students and the community. Applicants should demonstrate interest and a level of engagement with the aesthetic influences of the African Diaspora.The successful candidate will join the Visual Arts department during a time of growth. Morehouse College, together with Spelman College and Clark Atlanta University, is part of the Atlanta University Center Art History + Curatorial Studies Collective, now entering its seventh year. The Collective has positioned the AUC as a leading incubator of African American artists and museum professionals in the United States. We offers majors and minors in Art, Art History, and Curatorial Studies through coursework and co-curricular opportunities on all three campuses.Candidates must have a proven track record of art shows and artistic scholarship at the local or national level and be able to demonstrate interdisciplinary and creative approaches in teaching studio art and art appreciation courses with an interest in art of the African Diaspora and African American art and artists.Applicants are required to have an M.F.A. in Studio Art with a concentration in one of the following disciplines: Painting and drawing, Printmaking, Sculpture (including ceramics) or Photography and a minimum of three years of teaching experience in higher education beyond graduate school. In addition to studio art courses, the instructor will teach foundational courses (lecture based) relating to a general understanding of art for non-majors. The material taught in these courses should demonstrate an engagement with influences of the African Diaspora, inclusive of Afro-Futurism, Afro-Surrealism, Black Feminism, LGBTQ issues and/or other formal inquiries into and around the Black experience.This position also requires engagement in the department, the HSSMA Division and the College and a commitment to the mission of Morehouse College—to develop men with disciplined minds who lead lives of leadership and service by emphasizing the intellectual and character development of its students and by assuming a special responsibility for teaching the history and culture of Black people.An official transcript will be required of the selected candidate. Applicants are also asked to identify their strengths and experiences in assisting Black students and men of color from diverse cultural and socio-economic backgrounds to accomplish curricular goals.Questions may be directed to the Department Chair at Visual.arts@morehouse.edu Required Qualifications An M.F.A. in Studio Art with a concentration in one of the following disciplines: Painting and drawing, Printmaking, Sculpture (including ceramics) or Photography. A minimum of three years of teaching experience in higher education beyond graduate school. Preferred Qualifications Experience in or knowledge of related professions such as gallery administration and curatorial studies. Preferred Education/Experience Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities Knowledge of specific academic discipline for the instruction of the academic major. Job Title: Assistant/Associate Professor, Human-Centered Information Design & Technology Department: Human-Centered Information Design and Technology College/Division: School Of Engineering Primary Job Posting Location: Macon, GA 31207 Additional Job Posting Locations: (Other locations that this position could be based) Job Details: The Department of Human-Centered Information Design & Technology in the School of Engineering at Mercer University invites applications for a tenure-track faculty position at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor, to begin Fall 2027. We seek a colleague whose teaching, scholarship, and/or professional experience reflect the evolving landscape of human-centered, technical, and professional communication in contemporary workplaces. We are particularly interested in candidates whose expertise engages the creation, evaluation, management, and governance of information in complex, technology-mediated, digital, and AI-supported environments. Areas of Emphasis Areas of emphasis should align with the department’s strengths in technical communication, user experience, and artificial intelligence and may include one or more of the following: Accessibility and inclusive design Artificial intelligence and emerging communication technologies Collaborative workflows and project management Content strategy and User experience (UX) Human-computer interaction (HCI) and/or human-robot interaction (HRI) Information design and digital content practices Instructional design and learning experience design International and intercultural communication Technical and professional communication in high-tech environments Technical writing and editing Web design, development, and docs as code Position and Department The Department of Human-Centered Information Design & Technology offers undergraduate and graduate programs that prepare students for careers in technical, professional, digital, and user-centered communication. Located within the School of Engineering, the department provides a distinctive interdisciplinary environment at the intersection of communication, design, technology, and applied problem-solving. The department offers bachelor’s and master’s degree programs, as well as minors in technical communication, user experience, and artificial intelligence, and it provides service courses that support students across the School of Engineering. Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School Welcomes Alicia Hughes as Associate Dean of Student Affairs
jobs.description: September 11, 2026 Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School (AJMLS) is pleased to welcome Alicia Hughes as the new Associate Dean of Student Affairs. As an attorney, educator, higher education leader, and former public official, Hughes brings a distinguished career spanning legal practice, public service, academia, and student development. Dean Hughes will work directly with Dr. Harrison, who has entered her new role as the Senior Associate Dean and Chief of Student Affairs at AJMLS. Hughes began her academic career at Texas Southern University, where she earned a B.S. in Biology with dual minors in Chemistry and Biomedical Engineering. As an undergraduate, she was a Douglass Honors Institute Scholar, international champion debater, Student Government Association President, and National Institutes of Health undergraduate researcher at Baylor College of Medicine. She later earned her Juris Doctor from the University of Miami School of Law, where she held several leadership and academic positions, including serving as President of the Black Law Students Association. Her career has since taken her across law, government, public service, and higher education. After practicing law and completing a federal judicial clerkship with the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Alabama, Hughes went on to serve as a congressional staffer, elected city councilor, governor-appointed commissioner, and Chief Policy Advisor of the National Bar Association. Hughes has also built a significant career in legal education. She has taught at the University of Texas at Austin, Widener University’s Delaware Law School, Boston University School of Law, and Emory University School of Law, where she primarily taught and advised students in patent law. At Emory, she also served as the inaugural Executive Director of the Center on Civil Rights and Social Justice. Her academic and leadership experience includes fellowships with the University of Virginia’s Sorensen Institute for Political Leadership and the Aspen Institute’s Rodel Fellowship in Public Leadership. She has also completed doctoral coursework toward an Executive Ed.D. in Higher Education Management at the University of Pennsylvania. Now at AJMLS, Hughes is focused on building upon the strong foundation already established within Student Affairs while helping students navigate the many dimensions of their law school experience. Her vision encompasses academic success, wellness, belonging, professional identity, leadership, mentorship, service, and career preparation. “I am most excited about the opportunity to help shape a student affairs experience that sees each student not only as a law student, but as a whole person and an emerging legally-trained professional across a broad array of fields and vocational disciplines.” For Hughes, law school represents more than preparation for an examination or a first position. It is a formative period in which students begin developing the judgment, confidence, relationships, and professional identity that will shape their careers and lives. As Associate Dean, she hopes to make the Office of Student Affairs a place where students feel both supported and challenged. Her approach emphasizes individualized pathways into the profession and recognizes that professional readiness requires more than academic achievement alone. Mentorship, communication, professional etiquette, emotional intelligence, resilience, and preparation all play an important role in helping students take advantage of opportunities when they arise. “I want every student to have a solid pathway into the legal profession and to be poised and prepared to ‘meet the moment’ when opportunity arrives.” A central part of Hughes’ philosophy can be summed up through three questions she hopes students will be able to answer throughout their law school journey: Where am I now? Where am I going? And what do I need to do next? Through those questions, she hopes students will identify their strengths a

jobs.title: Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School Welcomes an Array of New Faculty for Fall 2026
jobs.description: August 31, 2026 Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School (AJMLS) is pleased to welcome an accomplished group of new faculty members for the Fall 2026 semester. Bringing decades of experience across litigation, family law, intellectual property, entertainment and media law, and other areas of practice, these attorneys offer students valuable perspectives drawn from both the courtroom and the legal profession. Their diverse backgrounds and professional expertise will enrich the classroom experience and help prepare AJMLS students to navigate the evolving legal landscape. Get to know the newest members of the AJMLS faculty below. Megan Boyd Legal Writing Instructor Megan E. Boyd is a lawyer, legal writing scholar, and educator. Before entering academia, she practiced in Atlanta, where she focused on insurance coverage and bad-faith litigation. She also served as a law clerk to the Honorable Asha F. Jackson of the United States District Court for the Northern District of Georgia. Boyd later joined the faculty of Georgia State University College of Law, where she taught legal research and writing, advanced legal writing, civil procedure, and professional responsibility. Boyd’s scholarship focuses on legal writing, advocacy, and legal education. She has published extensively in law reviews and bar journals and serves as Editor-in-Chief of the Scribes Journal of Legal Writing. Her work explores effective legal communication, persuasive advocacy, and the development of practical writing skills for lawyers. Boyd earned a Ph.D. in English from Georgia State University. Her dissertation, Law, Legitimacy, and Authority in Lewis Carroll, examines questions of law and governance in Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland, Through the Looking-Glass, and The Hunting of the Snark. Anthony Cochran Adjunct Professor Anthony (Tony) L. Cochran is an Atlanta attorney with more than 50 years of experience representing individuals and businesses in complex civil, criminal, administrative, and regulatory matters. He has tried dozens of jury and bench trials in both federal and state courts, as well as administrative, regulatory, and medical peer review proceedings. His broad trial experience allows him to navigate matters involving parallel civil, administrative, and criminal proceedings. Cochran is a Fellow of the American College of Trial Lawyers and regularly participates in continuing legal education programs and seminars. He has presented on a range of topics, including summary evidence under Federal Rule of Evidence 1006, the application of Daubert to expert testimony, representation of physicians, white-collar criminal defense, and internal investigations. He has also served as Chair and Director of the Zaban Paradies Center, an organization that assists homeless couples with obtaining housing and employment. Cochran began his legal career in Atlanta with Powell, Goldstein, Frazer & Murphy after graduating magna cum laude from Northwestern University Law School in 1976. From 1982 to 1985, he served as an Assistant United States Attorney for the Northern District of Georgia, where he prosecuted a variety of criminal cases and received commendations from the U.S. Attorney General and the Director of the FBI. He later served as an Adjunct Faculty Member at Emory University School of Law from 1986 to 2000. Peter Duitsman Adjunct Professor Peter J. Duitsman is Of Counsel at Smith Entertainment Law Group, where he provides legal and business affairs support to clients across the media, sports, and entertainment industries. He advises content creators, platforms, studios, and distributors on the development, acquisition, production, and monetization of content. Previously, Duitsman served as Senior Vice President and Associate General Counsel at Turner Broadcasting, WarnerMedia, and Warner Bros. Fort Valley State University, the only 1890 land-grant university in Georgia, is a comprehensive institution that provides an education to over 2,800 students including graduate students. The university is located in the town of Fort Valley in Peach County, the original site of the state's peach industry. Its 1,365-acre (5.52 km2) campus is Georgia's second-largest public university in area. Fort Valley State University is an equal opportunity employer. The University does not discriminate in employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or University System of Georgia policy. JOB SUMMARY: This position is responsible for directing the operations of the Nursing academic department in the College of Arts and & Sciences. The position is a 12-month tenure track position with academic rank commensurate with education, experience, and expertise. ESSENTIAL DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: Coordinates the department's accreditation activities to ensure continued approval by the Accreditation Commission for Education in Nursing (ACEN) and the Georgia Board of Nursing. Oversees curriculum development and revisions, including the preparation and submission of substantive change reports to accrediting agencies. Ensures clinical contracts are current and maintained with affiliated clinical agencies. Secures and schedules clinical site placements for nursing students enrolled in clinical courses. Oversees annual assessment and reporting initiatives. Oversees the student admissions process. Directs student orientation and academic advising. Addresses and resolves student appeals and complaints. Approves course schedules and revises them as needed. Monitors student enrollment during registration periods. Maintains departmental statistics, including the number of class sections and average class sizes. Plans and leads department faculty meetings. Recruit, hire, observe, and evaluate the performance of the nursing faculty and staff. Counsels faculty and staff regarding job performance and work-related responsibilities as needed. Approves faculty and staff work schedules, leave requests, and faculty development reimbursement requests in a timely manner. Oversees departmental and grant budgets. Allocates funds for equipment purchases and other departmental needs. Attends and/or ensures departmental representation at recruitment-related events. Represents the department at meetings scheduled by the Dean, Provost, or other university administrators. Instructs courses as needed. Serves on university committees as assigned. Performs other duties as assigned by the Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences. Serve as representative to university administration regarding all activities of the nursing program. Monitor nursing faculty continued professional development. Develop, maintain, and enhance relationships with partner health care facilities. Job Title: Director of Medical Practice, and Faculty Department: Internal Medicine College/Division: School Of Medicine Primary Job Posting Location: Macon, GA 31207 Additional Job Posting Locations: (Other locations that this position could be based) Job Details: Mercer University School of Medicine is searching for a non-tenure track Clinical Faculty position to serve as Director of Medical Practice. Rank to be determined based on the credentials of the selected candidate. Responsibilities : The Mercer University School of Medicine is seeking a highly qualified educator with a passion for teaching thorough history and physical exam skills. This position is available on the Macon campus. This teaching position will play a key role in planning for 2nd year curriculum including all clinical skills practices, practicums and final exams. This M.D. will give lectures or recruit faculty to provide overviews as directed in the curriculum and lead practice sessions. This position will need to oversee and grade any written assignments and clinical investigation curriculum as well as remediate students as needed. Coordination with the Directors of Medical Practice and the entire Medical Practice Team on the Columbus and Savannah campuses is key. For over thirty years, MUSM has focused on training medical students to fulfill MUSM’s mission of preparing healthcare professionals to meet the primary care and health care needs of rural and underserved Georgia residents and communities. The HSSMA Division is home to 11 Departments, 4 Academic Programs, 20 majors, over 75 full-time faculty and 4 Endowed Chairs. We are seeking a new faculty member who specializes in the social and cultural determinants of health for the ever-growing share of the global population who live in cities. While cities can create opportunities for health, urban living can also adversely impact the health and wellness of communities. Candidates whose work brings urban health to the policy-making table and whose scholarship addresses one or more of the following areas are encouraged to apply: The intersection of health inequities and racial injustice The impacts of urban policies or new technologies on health and well-being Mapping the health impacts of urban infrastructure (transportation, land-use, energy and housing) Applicants should have an established record of contributions to innovative solutions to social problems in Black communities, multidisciplinary scholarship and experience working across sectors and institutions. jobs.title: Faculty Research
jobs.description: Faculty Research Bridging Scholarship and ServiceClark Atlanta University’s faculty are committed to research with a purpose. Whether in scientific labs, policy forums, or artistic venues, they continue to push forward new knowledge while directly engaging and benefiting the communities around them. Their work not only advances public health, scholarship, and creative expression but also carries forward the University’s legacy of fostering social change, civic leadership, and cultural enrichment in the African American community. Get the latest updates Groundbreaking Cancer ResearchCAU’s Center for Cancer Research and Therapeutic Development (CCRTD) received an $11 million renewal grant from NIH’s NIMHD to expand what is one of the nation’s largest prostate cancer programs. This five-year award supports three new translational research projects targeting prostate cancer in African-American men, upgrades to research facilities, and enhanced community engagement in prostate cancer education.The investment builds on CCRTD’s mission to eradicate prostate cancer health disparities through cutting-edge research and outreach.Learn more about the grantDepartment of Defense Prostate Cancer ProgramWe have received funding from the Department of Defense Congressionally Directed Medical Research Program in Prostate Cancer for two projects.Intracrine Regulation of Androgen Receptor in Prostate Cancer CellsDr. Shafiq A. Khan (CCRTD Director) leads the “Intracrine Regulation of Androgen Receptor in Prostate Cancer Cells” study, which examines how prostate tumors may produce their own testosterone to resist standard hormone therapy, aiming to improve treatment for both androgen-dependent and -independent cancers. Such work could inform new combination therapies to more fully starve tumors of growth signals in later-stage disease.Snail-mediated Signaling in Human Prostate CancerDr. Valerie Odero-Marah, CCRTD associate professor, investigates the molecular drivers of prostate cancer spread. Her project, “Snail-mediated Signaling in Human Prostate Cancer,” focuses on the Snail transcription factor, which promotes epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT), a process linked to metastasis. By studying how Snail contributes to EMT and neuroendocrine changes in prostate tumors, this research seeks new strategies to halt aggressive, metastatic prostate cancers. Such insights are vital for developing therapies to prevent lethal disease progression. Civic Engagement and Public Policy InitiativesLegislative AnalysisThe Georgia Legislative Review (GLR), produced by CAU’s W.E.B. Du Bois Southern Center for Studies in Public Policy, is an annual faculty-led analysis of Georgia’s legislative session. It provides an in-depth review of major state bills and policy decisions each year, with special attention to issues affecting marginalized communities and has quickly become a valuable resource for scholars, citizens, and advocates seeking to understand and influence policy in the American South.Uniquely, the GLR “grades” state legislators on their voting records by evaluating how those votes impact the quality of life for Black Georgians. In doing so, the review highlights outcomes in areas such as voting rights, redistricting, social justice, housing, and education, holding policymakers accountable to the Black community’s interests.Read the GLR“Status of Black Atlanta” Urban Policy StudyCAU’s Du Bois Center is leading a comprehensive study on the State of Black Atlanta, examining critical challenges faced by Black residents in the city. Each section assesses inequities (e.g. achievement gaps in schools, income and job barriers, healthcare access, affordable housing shortages, and racial disparities in policing and sentencing). By spotlighting these issues, the report serves as a call to action for policymakers and stakeholders to enact reforms and investments that improve quality of life for Black Atlantans.The study’s ultimate goal is to inform urban policy s

Responsibilities : This position is a non-tenure track, 12-month appointment on the Columbus, GA campus. Additional duties will be required/assigned during the summer. Teaching faculty will play a key role in the continued development and implementation of an integrated, cross-disciplinary curriculum that includes small and large group case-based and team-based learning, and other active teaching-learning methods. Expertise in other disciplines will also be considered depending on the teaching needs of our department. Qualifications : Candidates must hold a terminal degree (M.D or equivalent, Ph.D.) from an accredited college/university in an appropriate discipline. Job Title: Faculty, Clinical Psychology Department: Clinical Psychology College/Division: College Of Health Professions Primary Job Posting Location: Atlanta, GA 30341 Additional Job Posting Locations: (Other locations that this position could be based) Job Details: The College of Health Professions at Mercer University invites applications for a full-time faculty member for the Doctor of Psychology Program. This position is for a tenure-track faculty in a progressive and innovative department that emphasizes evidence-based treatment, an integrative approach to healthcare, and interaction with our other partner programs (Physical Therapy, Physician Assistant Studies, Public Health, Athletic Training, and Kinesiology). Rank will be determined based on the credentials of the selected candidate. Responsibilities Responsibilities include doctoral student classroom instruction and evaluation; small group support for clinical training; advisement and mentoring of students; admissions and accreditation activities; committee involvement; and scholarly activities to include publications, grants, presentations, and collaborative projects. Successful candidates will demonstrate a strong commitment to excellence in teaching, clinical training, and student mentorship within a practitioner-scholar model. The ideal candidates also will have a strong research orientation with established or potential for extramural support. As a faculty member at Mercer University, you can expect to be immersed into a community of scholars who are committed to excellence. Qualifications General qualifications include a degree from an APA-accredited PhD or PsyD Clinical Psychology program and completion of an APA-accredited internship. Active, unrestricted license to practice as a clinical psychologist in Georgia or immediate eligibility is required. Prior experience teaching, supervising, and mentoring graduate students is preferred. Preference for this position will be given to someone with expertise and teaching experience in Cognitive Assessment . A background in clinical neuropsychology, with the ability to teach Neuropsychological Assessment and Biological Bases of Behavior , is also desirable. Other areas of expertise within clinical psychology will be considered. Additional Information This position will be a 12-month appointment based at Mercer University’s Cecil B. Day campus in Atlanta, Georgia, conveniently located near all the amenities of the city and situation on over 250 wooded acres. More information can be found at http://www.mercer.edu/ . Questions regarding this position may be directed to Dr. Michelle Robbins, robbins_mm@mercer.edu , 678.547.6225. Interested applicants will need to complete the brief online application and attach a letter of interest, current curriculum vitae, teaching philosophy, description of research agenda, and the names and contact information for three references. Review of applications will begin immediately. Background Check Contingencies: - Criminal History

jobs.description: JobsLogin Back to all jobsLecturer - Business - Hospitality (Non-Tenure Track)Posted 08-Jul-2026 (EST)643 Martin Luther King Junior Drive Southwest, Atlanta, GA 30314, USASalaryFull Time Email Me Similar Jobs Email Me This Job LECTURER – BUSINESS (Hospitality) (NON-TENURE TRACK) Department of Business Morris Brown College · Atlanta, Georgia OVERVIEW Morris Brown College invites applications for a part-time, non-tenure track Lecturer in the Department of Business. The successful candidate will report to the Department Chair and support the mission of Academic Affairs. This position carries a teaching load of five (5) courses each semester, delivered face-to-face and/or synchronously, and includes academic advising and institutional service responsibilities. JOB DUTIES Job duties include, but are not limited to, the following requirements as defined by TRACS accreditation standards, the board-approved Faculty Handbook, administrative policies, and state requirements set forth by The Georgia Nonpublic Postsecondary Education Commission (GNPEC). Faculty members are expected to be effective teachers and excel in course instruction. The minimum expectations of faculty who teach at Morris Brown College are outlined below: Teaching Effectiveness Possess thorough and accurate knowledge of the specific field or discipline, including the ability to evaluate and apply content Select and develop instructional materials; jobs.title: Professor Erin Corken Publishes Two-Part Series on AI Ethics and Legal Practice
jobs.description: September 11, 2026 Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School (AJMLS) congratulates Professor Erin Corken on the recent publication of her two-part scholarly series, The Two Letters That Matter Most in the Future of Legal Practice: And They’re Not What You Think — Automation Bias, ABA Formal Opinion 512, and the Emerging Ethical Framework for AI-Assisted Legal Work, published in PLI Current: The Journal of PLI Press, Vol. 10 (2026). The two-part series examines the ethical responsibilities of legal professionals using artificial intelligence in legal practice, with particular attention to automation bias, ABA Formal Opinion 512, the evolving sanctions landscape surrounding AI misuse, and the practical considerations attorneys must address when incorporating AI tools into their work. In Part I, Corken explores the technology underlying generative and agentic AI, the cognitive risks associated with automation and confirmation bias, and the ethical duties implicated by AI-assisted legal work. The article provides an in-depth examination of ABA Formal Opinion 512 and its application to professional obligations involving competence, confidentiality, communication, candor toward the tribunal, supervision, and fees. Part II examines the consequences when those obligations are not followed, beginning with Mata v. Avianca and tracing the increasing sanctions imposed in cases involving AI-generated errors. Corken then turns to the human dimension of AI use, including the potential erosion of professional expertise and the importance of independent judgment and what she describes as “inner knowing.” The article concludes with practical guidance for attorneys, emphasizing jurisdiction-specific requirements, organizational AI policies, human oversight, and independent verification of AI-generated work. Corken’s scholarship emphasizes a central principle: AI can assist legal professionals, but it cannot replace the professional judgment and accountability of the attorney. Her analysis encourages practitioners to approach AI-assisted work with careful verification and a willingness to reject unreliable output when necessary. The abstract for the two-part series reads: “This two-part series discusses the ethical framework, challenges, and professional obligations surrounding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in legal practice. The article analyzes automation bias, ABA Formal Opinion 512, evolving sanctions for AI misuse, and provides practical guidance for legal professionals to responsibly integrate AI tools while maintaining ethical standards and competence. Everyone in the legal profession is talking about two letters: AI. But the two letters that matter most in the future of legal practice are not AI. They are NO, the most underused and most essential word in the age of artificial intelligence. This article examines why, through the lens of automation bias, ABA Formal Opinion 512 (July 29, 2024), a rapidly growing body of sanctions case law, state bar ethics opinions, and court rules. As of June 2026, more than thirty states have issued formal AI ethics guidance, courts from the Southern District of Texas to the Ninth Circuit have developed local rules and issued landmark decisions, and the sanctions for AI-related errors have grown from modest fines to professional suspensions and disqualifications. Automation bias, the cognitive tendency at the root of nearly every ethical failure in AI-assisted legal practice, runs through all of it. This article provides a complete analysis of Opinion 512, a survey of the evolving landscape since its issuance, practical guidance for practitioners, and a framework for understanding why the most important professional skill in the age of AI is not knowing how to use the technology. It is knowing when to say no to what it tells you.” Professor Corken’s scholarship reflects her interdisciplinary experience in law, legal technology, e-discovery, privacy, and cybersecurity. She is an attorney licensed in Kent

jobs.title: Professor Jonathan Rapping Speaks to High School Students at Gate City Bar Association’s Justice Robert Benham Law Camp
jobs.description: June 29, 2026 Atlanta’s John Marshall Law School (AJMLS) Professor Jonathan Rapping recently spoke to high school students at the Gate City Bar Association’s Twentieth Annual Justice Robert Benham Law Camp, held at Georgia State University College of Law. Professor Rapping, Faculty Director of the Criminal and Civil Justice Institute (CCJI), addressed students as part of the camp’s programming designed to introduce high school participants to the legal profession and issues of justice and equity. During his presentation, he spoke about social justice lawyering and the need for lawyers committed to building a more humane legal system. He highlighted CCJI’s work to prepare a generation of attorneys dedicated to advancing equal justice and strengthening fairness within legal institutions. Professor Rapping also discussed the challenges that can arise for lawyers practicing in systems that may feel impersonal, emphasizing the importance of maintaining empathy, purpose and professional resilience throughout a legal career. The Justice Robert Benham Law Camp, an annual program of the Gate City Bar Association, brings together high school students from across the Atlanta area for legal education, mentorship, and exposure to the justice system. This year’s session featured strong student engagement, with many participants expressing interest in pursuing law and further involvement in justice-related work.

jobs.title: Professor Lance McMillian Discusses Writing and AI at Georgia Supreme Court and Court of Appeals
jobs.description: July 23, 2026 Professor Lance McMillian, creator of the best-selling Atlanta Murder Squad crime series, recently appeared at the Georgia Supreme Court and Court of Appeals to discuss the craft of writing and the rise of artificial intelligence to summer interns working in both courts. Justice Carla Wong McMillian of the Supreme Court hosted the event. Drawing on his experience as a civil litigator, legal scholar, and novelist, Professor McMillian provided his audience a series of tips for becoming powerful legal writers. These insights included the importance of knowing your intended audience, how to add meaningful value to your work in a world where attention spans are shorter than ever, and embracing the power of story as a tool of persuasion. Professor McMillian also discussed the limits of artificial intelligence in creating written product, emphasizing the continuing importance of lawyers utilizing their legal judgment to craft arguments that move people. The event marks the second consecutive summer Professor McMillian has been invited to lecture to the interns. Death to the Chief, Professor McMillian’s second novel, revolves around the murder of the Chief Justice of the Georgia Supreme Court, leading to a number of questions from the students about the creative process and the line between fiction and reality. In addition to Death to the Chief, Professor McMillian has published six novels in the last five years: The Murder of Sara Barton, To Kill a Lawyer, A Hard Way to Die, The Just and the Unjust, Street Girls, A Town on Trial, and the recently-released Prescription for Homicide. His books have reached best-seller status on Kindle, Audible Plus, Apple Books, and Nook, including holding the position as the #1 Best-Selling Legal Thriller in the world. His scholarly work has appeared in leading journals such as the North Carolina Law Review, the Wisconsin Law Review, the Washington and Lee Law Review, the Alabama Law Review, and many others.
